This is the second repeat bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail.

sentences.text: Penal Code of 1860 read with Section 5(G), 5(L) and 6 of POCSO Act.

As per prosecution story, on 16.06.2022, father of the prosecutrix lodged an FIR at P.S. Ranapur,
District Jhabua by stating that his minor daughter (prosecutrix) was abducted by the present applicant and other co-accused persons in a Bolero vehicle.
They took her in forest, there present applicant committed rape upon her.
Accordingly, offence has been registered.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 20.06.2022.
After rejecting his earlier bail application prosecutrix (PW-1), her father (PW-2), aunt (PW-3) and mother (PW-4) have been examined before the trial Court.
All of them have turned hostile and have not stated anything against the present applicant regarding the aforementioned offence.
Applicant is permanent resident of Alirajpur district.
Applicant is a young person aged about 20 years.
Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Hence, he prays that present applicant be enlarged on bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.
Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix has been examined before the trial Court and she has categorically stated in her statement that present applicant neither abducted nor committed rape upon her; her father (PW-2), aunt (PW-3) and mother (PW-4) have also been deposed in the same manner but final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.
In view of the above, without commenting upon the merits of the case, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, the application is allowed.

It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Anushree Guddu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90476047/
